items.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: He has performed and recorded with Bucky Pizzarelli, John Bunch and Ruby Braff

ctx.x: Harry Allen is one of the promising young players keeping the tradition of mainstream jazz alive. He was born in Washington, DC in 1966 and raised in Rhode Island, and he was introduced to jazz through his father's record collection. The accordion was his first instrument but he was drawn to the tenor saxophone after hearing Scott Hamilton. Harry's impact on the jazz scene has been considerable. He has performed and recorded with Bucky Pizzarelli, John Bunch and Ruby Braff, and he appears at numerous festivals…
Harry was interviewed by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive, at the Allegheny Jazz Festival in Chautauqua, New York on September 13, 1997.

items.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Well there’s a new guy that I have worked with that I find is just a delightful guy to play with... And his name is Harry Allen.

ctx.x: Are there any other musicians that you played with that you shared a particularly fun or fulfilling experience with?

Well there’s a new guy that I have worked with that I find is just a delightful guy to play with and he’s only 27 years old and he’s also my tennis — he’s the guy that ruined my wrist. We played tennis together. He lives right across the river. I live right in Manhattan and he lives right across the river and I get in my car and drive over and play tennis with him whenever I can. And his name is Harry Allen. You ever heard of him by any chance?
